propositions: rebar comment accepts flag-looking tokens (e.g., --body-file, --body) as positional body arguments and stores them literally instead of rejecting them, silently destroying the intended content while exiting with code 0
a body argument beginning with a dash is accepted and stored as-is rather than rejected with an error and usage guidance

positional-body commands (comment, create, edit, session-log, tag, untag, archive, set-verify-commands) lack consistent validation to reject flag-like tokens, exposing the same silent-loss footgun across multiple commands
the -- escape hatch is documented and functional for legitimately dash-prefixed body values
an additional defect compounds the loss: surplus positional arguments are discarded via args[:min_args] slicing, so rebar comment <id> --body-file notes.md loses the body twice and still exits 0
